doc_eb25fc5bc7a1:N1.label: Gecko toe pad
doc_eb25fc5bc7a1:N1.description: The adhesive organ on gecko feet containing hierarchical microstructures

doc_eb25fc5bc7a1:N2.label: Keratin seta
doc_eb25fc5bc7a1:N2.description: Hair-like keratin structure approximately 100 micrometers long

doc_eb25fc5bc7a1:N3.label: Spatula
doc_eb25fc5bc7a1:N3.description: Nanoscale terminal structure (~200 nm) at the tip of each seta branch

doc_eb25fc5bc7a1:N4.label: Hierarchical structure (lamella → seta → spatula)
doc_eb25fc5bc7a1:N4.description: Multi-level branching architecture from lamellae to setae to spatulae

doc_eb25fc5bc7a1:N5.label: Maximized contact area
doc_eb25fc5bc7a1:N5.description: Large effective surface area achieved through hierarchical branching

doc_eb25fc5bc7a1:N6.label: Van der Waals forces
doc_eb25fc5bc7a1:N6.description: Intermolecular forces between spatulae and substrate surface

doc_eb25fc5bc7a1:N7.label: Dry adhesion
doc_eb25fc5bc7a1:N7.description: Adhesion without chemical bonding or wet adhesive, relying solely on intermolecular forces

doc_eb25fc5bc7a1:N8.label: Intermolecular forces
doc_eb25fc5bc7a1:N8.description: Fundamental attractive forces between molecules at the spatula-surface interface

doc_eb25fc5bc7a1:N9.label: Adhesion strength ~10 N/cm²
doc_eb25fc5bc7a1:N9.description: Quantitative measure of adhesive force per unit area

doc_eb25fc5bc7a1:N10.label: Reversible adhesion
doc_eb25fc5bc7a1:N10.description: Ability to repeatedly attach and detach without residue or degradation

doc_eb25fc5bc7a1:N11.label: Peeling toes at an angle
doc_eb25fc5bc7a1:N11.description: Active detachment behavior where gecko lifts toes at a specific angle

doc_eb25fc5bc7a1:N12.label: Breaking van der Waals interaction
doc_eb25fc5bc7a1:N12.description: Separation of spatulae from surface by overcoming intermolecular forces

evidence: Gecko toe pads have millions of keratin setae
Each seta branches into hundreds of spatulae
The hierarchical structure (lamella → seta → spatula) maximizes contact area.
intermolecular forces amplified by enormous contact area
The adhesion mechanism is van der Waals forces between the spatulae and the surface.
The key feature is dry adhesion — no chemical bonding, no wet adhesive, just intermolecular forces amplified by enormous contact area.
the gecko peels its toes at an angle to break the van der Waals interaction
Reversible: the gecko peels its toes at an angle to break the van der Waals interaction.
